hypothesis: constraining the fast small model to extractive output (closed-enum country, query-substring keywords, deterministic search_terms) aligns its output space with what drives retrieval and recovers retrieval fidelity
accuracy_metric: retrieval fidelity vs gemma baseline ranked doc IDs
finding: Output constraints do not recover retrieval fidelity. Enum-constraining country barely moved country agreement (0.690->0.705), so the country divergence is semantic (the two models choose differently), not a formatting/normalization artifact. With keywords and search_terms also constrained to be extractive, Recall stayed ~0.34 (unchanged from free generation). Therefore the extraction->retrieval divergence between two different models is model-intrinsic, not an output-form artifact, and cannot be cheaply aligned. Non-obvious implication: accuracy-preserving acceleration must keep the SAME model on the retrieval-driving path; the viable levers are same-model harness changes (remove/parallelize calls) and output-lossless serving-level decode acceleration (speculative decoding / tensor parallelism), not model substitution or constrained fast extraction.
